entry.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
entry.summary:
We study high-probability linear regression in the infinite variance regime, wherecthe regression noise has only a finite conditional $α$-moment $ν$ for some unknown $α\in(1,2)$, and the covariates may only have finite moments up to a given order (e.g., 4th moment). We give a black-box reduction that converts finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures. The reduction is based on empirical residual pruning and is agnostic to the moment exponent, the noise scale, the covariance, and the design moment. Under a finite fourth-moment condition on the covariates, any finite-variance subroutine attaining the sub-Gaussian rate yields the following when the number of samples $n$ is above a suitably defined threshold: Without knowing $α$ or $ν$, we have with probability at least $1-δ$ that $ \|\widehatθ-θ^*\|_Σ
  \lesssim_α
  ν^{1/α}
  \big(\frac{d+\log(1/δ)}{n}\big)^{\frac{α-1}α}, $ where $d$ is the dimension, $Σ$ is the covariate covariance matrix, and $\|v\|_Σ:=(v^\topΣv)^{1/2}$. We further prove a matching minimax lower bound that holds under the same conditions. The reduction is computationally efficient whenever the finite-variance subroutine is. We also obtain a distribution-free prediction guarantee under a bounded raw $α$-moment assumption on the response, and give an analogous $α$-agnostic reduction for mean estimation.

entry.title: Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang
entry.summary: The first stars formed out of light elements (H, He, and Li leftover from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis) and began the chemical enrichment of the Universe. Identifying this first-generation population of stars, known as Population III, and understanding their properties is one of the most ambitious goals of modern extragalactic astrophysics. We report the detection of He and H emission lines and extremely low Oxygen abundance in AMORE6, a strongly magnified galaxy at redshift z = 5.725, i.e. approximately one billion years after the Big Bang, with deep James Webb Space Telescope spectroscopy. He II lambda1640 and lambda4686 emission lines are detected at 16.7 sigma and 4.0 sigma significance, respectively. The observed He II-to-Hbeta ratios are consistent with predictions for extreme ionizing radiation fields and the low chemical compositions typical of Population III stars. Oxygen abundance of the interstellar medium is estimated to be 8 x 10^-4 solar from weak [OIII]lambda4363 and lambda5008 lines, consistent with an almost pristine environment, perhaps enriched by the Pop III stars themselves. Although we cannot exclude alternative sources of hard ionizing radiation, such as accreting black holes, these observations offer the first view of the extremely low metallicity environment where the Universe's first stars are predicted to be born. The data show that such pockets of pristine gas still exist one billion years after the Big Bang and that they are dominated by very massive stars.

entry.title: A Methodologically Rigorous Benchmark of Linear Regression,RNN, and LSTM for S&P 500 Forecasting:Identifying Sources of Performance Inflation in Financial DeepLearning
entry.summary: This study examines one-day-ahead forecasting of the S&P 500 closing level using a 2006-2025 dataset that includes fundamental price data, macroeconomic indicators, and engineered technical features. We benchmark three model families, namely linear regression, vanilla recurrent neural networks (RNN), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM), within a unified preprocessing and chronological evaluation pipeline. A central contribution of this work is a methodological audit of common practices in the deep-learning-for-stock-prediction literature. We identify three sources of result inflation that frequently appear in published methodologies: wavelet-denoised evaluation targets, the absence of a naive persistence baseline, and best-of-N replicate reporting. We then re-evaluate all model families under a corrected protocol that controls for each. Performance is reported using root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, and the Pearson correlation coefficient, averaged across N = 30 independent replicates per configuration. We compare models on accuracy, stability across replicates, and architectural depth sensitivity, using the naive persistence forecast (predicting today's close as tomorrow's close) as a primary baseline against which all candidate models must demonstrate improvement.

entry.title: MemOnce: A Scalable Memory Architecture for Large Language Models
entry.summary: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313$\times$ and prefill latency by 6.9$\times$ at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5$\times$ and overall memory performance by +5.77%. Finally, MemOnce generalizes zero-shot to downstream representation tasks, achieving competitive results against specialized models.

entry.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
entry.summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, activity and impulse control. Electroencephalography (EEG) records brain activity as children and adolescents perform cognitive tasks. However, comparing features derived from these recordings requires consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows and documented quality decisions. We curated 669 existing BALLADEER recordings from 156 participants across five task conditions so that researchers can compare seven EEG feature families on the same time intervals for each participant and task. The dataset links continuous signals to precomputed measurements from 115 feature definitions or templates and records the quality decisions made for each recording. Analyses must still account for repeated measurements within participants, residual artefacts and differences between acquisition systems. Technical validation covered signal integrity, numerical checks on feature estimators and completeness of the released files. In every task, the median proportion of recording time retained after preprocessing was 100%. To illustrate reuse, we report saved participant-held-out evaluations comparing XGBoost using all seven families on eight-second windows with a predictor based only on recruitment-group prevalence in the training fold. Recruitment-group discrimination was stronger in Robots than in the three Slackline conditions. These descriptive results from overlapping cohorts do not establish diagnostic validity. The dataset, curation software and aggregate results for the predictive example are publicly available.

entry.title: Task2Hand: A Contact-Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous-Hand Morphology Design
entry.summary: Dexterous hand design demands repeated expert work across geometry, robot-description code, collision debugging, grasp initialization, and policy training. We present Task2Hand, a Skill: a specification package that turns a functional manipulation brief into a parameterized hand model and routes every candidate through cost-ordered contact, dynamics, and learning gates. Each gate returns a status and an evidence record; on failure, the Skill records the earliest blocker, revises one bounded parameter group, and reruns the cheaper gates. The agent generates, validates, and trains autonomously within declared bounds, and escalates trade-offs, plateaus, and conflicting evidence to a human who sets the next design direction. An evidence-driven design trajectory for bidirectional in-hand manipulation yielded SAGE Hand (Skill-Aware Generative Embodiment): four fingers, 16 actuated DoF, an integrated guiding palm, compact roots, cylindrical tips, and a collision-cleared opposable thumb. Under a matched training protocol, SAGE Hand reaches 45.6% task success on a hexagonal prism against 37.3% for the LEAP hand, and 70.8% on a bicolor cylinder against 51.6%. Dense simulated tactile input more than halves the cylinder drop rate. In a controlled iteration study, the Skill path preserves capture at 164/165 trials while the path without the Skill degrades to 14/165, confirming that the gates act as a regression guard during refinement. Accepted candidates pack with URDF/MJCF, metrics, checkpoints, and a provenance manifest.

entry.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata
entry.summary:
To prevent motion sensors from acting as covert microphones, Android 12+ caps SensorManager gyroscope and accelerometer rates at 200 Hz by default, requires HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS for higher rates, and throttles sensors back to 200 Hz when the microphone toggle is off. We show that Android's Camera2 subsystem bypasses these defenses. During an active Camera2 session, Camera HAL stabilization pipelines record high-rate gyroscope measurements and export them via vendor CaptureResult metadata. Loudspeaker speech excites chassis vibrations that couple into this path. Across 50 smartphones (2020-2026) from 10 vendors, 37 expose gyroscope metadata via Camera2, and 26 exceed 200 Hz--including six flagship models at 800-1000 Hz, double SensorManager's 400-500 Hz ceiling. This channel requires neither RECORD_AUDIO nor HIGH_SAMPLING_RATE_SENSORS and defeats privacy switches: turning off the microphone toggle does not throttle metadata, and turning off the camera toggle blanks only video frames while 800-1000 Hz metadata keeps streaming.
  To build a zero-profiling attack that generalizes to unseen phones, we introduce Source-to-Leakage Learning (S2L). Prior attacks train on real sensor traces, entangling speech with a specific phone's mechanical resonances and sampling rate. S2L decouples speech content from hardware acoustics using a physics-constrained forward simulator. Trained exclusively on simulated leakage without target-phone traces, our universal recognizer CamEar achieves 52.1% mean word accuracy (up to 61.8%) and 74.3% character accuracy (up to 80.7%) across the six 800-1000 Hz phones. In contrast, ISpyU models fine-tuned on real target-phone data drop to 25.9% word accuracy on unseen phones; CamEar improves cross-device accuracy by 101.4% and outperforms ISpyU's same-device models on every tested phone.

entry.title: Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology
entry.summary: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's own components during training -- freeing a smaller heterogeneous network inside. We evaluate Model Carving by pre-training standard Transformers from 140M to 2.7B parameters and looped Transformers from 140M to 1.3B. At equal training compute, carved models reach a lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Furthermore, carved models also outperform size-matched models produced by pruning or distillation, suggesting that the best way to obtain small models for edge devices is to carve them during training, not to compress a large one afterwards. This advantage both grows with scale and carries over to downstream tasks such as few-shot evaluation and generation. Because the removed sublayers no longer run, carved models also cost up to 34% fewer FLOPs per token and decode up to 1.6 times faster without cost in quality. Our results show that architecture, like weights, should be learned and not fixed in advance, and that inside every large transformer is a smaller, faster, stronger one waiting to be carved out.
entry.arxiv:comment: 38 pages, 15 figures, 19 tables. Under review at ICLR 2027. Project page: https://kadenzheng.com/model-carving/

entry.title: Explicational statistics: research for an AI age
entry.summary: AI is dramatically changing the statistical research landscape. I argue that production of a distinct category of statistical knowledge, which I refer to as explicational statistics, is actually becoming more valuable as AI increasingly automates other parts of the research process. I define explicational statistics, contextualize it in terms of other forms of statistical knowledge, and explain why I think the rise of AI makes it more valuable. I demonstrate my framework by first developing a new dimension reduction method, Ambient Embedding Projection, that can simultaneously visualize the intrinsic geometry of a data manifold along with how that manifold is embedded into ambient space. I then use my new method to conceive of a new statistical property of a collection of manifolds, related to metric distortion, that in single-cell biology can capture the ensemble behavior of cell populations. I apply these ideas to single-nuclei RNA-seq data from the brains of mice from different behavioral conditions to reveal potential cellular mechanisms of chronic social defeat stress.

entry.title: Ranking-Preserving Coreset Selection for Efficient Evolutionary Hyperparameter Optimization
entry.summary: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) is essential for high predictive performance, but its computational cost becomes prohibitive when candidate configurations require repeated training on large datasets. This paper proposes a ranking-preserving coreset (RPC) selection framework for accelerating evolutionary HPO. The method constructs a compact coreset that preserves the relative ranking of hyperparameter configurations observed on the full training data. Coreset selection is formulated as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes Spearman rank correlation between full-data and subset-based configuration rankings while penalizing subset size. The selected coreset is then used for HPO with three evolutionary algorithms: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Cross-generational elitist Selection, Heterogeneous Recombination and Cataclysmic Mutation (CHC), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Experiments on seven tabular, two text, and two image benchmark datasets show that RPC substantially reduces HPO time while maintaining test accuracy comparable to full-dataset HPO across decision tree, text classification, and image classification tasks. Across datasets and optimizers, HPO-stage speedups range from approximately 1.14x to 8.80x, while the one-time coreset construction cost is accounted for separately through end-to-end runtime and break-even analysis. On 20 held-out configurations excluded from coreset construction, RPC achieves higher ranking correlation than same-size random sampling on 8 of 11 datasets (dataset-level Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p = 0.014). These results show that ranking preservation extends beyond the configurations used during selection. The one-time construction cost can be amortized when the coreset is reused across HPO runs.
